## File: tauri-app/src/lib/document-store.ts
````typescript
import { invoke } from '@tauri-apps/api/core';

// Storage seam of the frontend. The feature code never calls Tauri commands
// directly; it goes through this document-store interface so a future backend
// can be swapped in one place. The default client persists JSON documents in
// the app-data directory through the Rust document commands, whose backend is
// selected by storage.json (backend: "local" | "mongodb").
export interface DocumentStoreClient {
  /** Returns null when the document does not exist. */
  read(filename: string): Promise<string | null>;
  write(filename: string, content: string): Promise<void>;
  remove(filename: string): Promise<void>;
  /** Lists document keys below the prefix, sorted. */
  list(prefix: string): Promise<string[]>;
}

export class LocalDocumentStore implements DocumentStoreClient {
  async read(filename: string): Promise<string | null> {
    try {
      return await invoke<string>('load_local_file', { filename });
    } catch {
      return null;
    }
  }

  async write(filename: string, content: string): Promise<void> {
    await invoke('save_local_file', { filename, content });
  }

  async remove(filename: string): Promise<void> {
    await invoke('delete_local_file', { filename });
  }

  async list(prefix: string): Promise<string[]> {
    try {
      return await invoke<string[]>('list_local_files', { prefix });
    } catch {
      return [];
    }
  }
}

// Single seam to extend: once the MongoDB backend exists (MongoDocumentStore
// on the Rust side, or a direct driver client), select it here - ideally by
// reading the same storage.json through a `get_storage_config` invoke.
export function createDocumentStore(): DocumentStoreClient {
  return new LocalDocumentStore();
}
````

## File: tauri-app/src/lib/light-simulation.ts
````typescript
export const LIGHT_COLORS = ['Red', 'Green', 'Blue', 'White'] as const;
export type LightColor = typeof LIGHT_COLORS[number];
export const DISPLAY_CHANNELS = ['Red', 'Green', 'Blue', 'RGB'] as const;
export type DisplayChannel = typeof DISPLAY_CHANNELS[number];

export type SimulationChannel = {
  index: number;
  value: number;
  angle: number;
  color: string;
  enable: boolean;
};

export type LightPageState = {
  enabled: boolean;
  channels: SimulationChannel[];
};

export type LightGains = {
  red: number;
  green: number;
  blue: number;
};

export type GvStatsLike = {
  mean: number;
  std: number;
  min: number;
  max: number;
  pixels: number;
  /** Raw MEDIAN luma counts; used to measure the simulated, clipped pixels. */
  histogram?: number[];
};

export const LIGHT_VALUE_MIN = 0;
export const LIGHT_VALUE_MAX = 1024;

export function clampLightValue(value: number): number {
  if (!Number.isFinite(value)) return LIGHT_VALUE_MIN;
  return Math.min(LIGHT_VALUE_MAX, Math.max(LIGHT_VALUE_MIN, Math.round(value)));
}

export function createLightPage(channels: readonly SimulationChannel[]): LightPageState {
  const normalized = channels.map((channel) => ({
    ...channel,
    value: clampLightValue(channel.value),
  }));
  return {
    enabled: normalized.some((channel) => channel.enable),
    channels: normalized,
  };
}

function colorKey(color: string): LightColor | null {
  const normalized = color.trim().toLowerCase();
  if (normalized === 'r' || normalized === 'red') return 'Red';
  if (normalized === 'g' || normalized === 'green') return 'Green';
  if (normalized === 'b' || normalized === 'blue') return 'Blue';
  if (normalized === 'w' || normalized === 'white') return 'White';
  return null;
}

function pageContribution(page: LightPageState, color: LightColor): number {
  const values = page.channels
    .filter((channel) => channel.enable && colorKey(channel.color) === color)
    .map((channel) => clampLightValue(channel.value));
  if (!values.length) return 0;
  return values.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0) / values.length / LIGHT_VALUE_MAX;
}

export function computeLightGains(pages: readonly LightPageState[], enabled: boolean): LightGains {
  if (!enabled) return { red: 1, green: 1, blue: 1 };
  let red = 1;
  let green = 1;
  let blue = 1;
  for (const page of pages.slice(0, 3)) {
    if (!page.enabled) continue;
    const white = pageContribution(page, 'White');
    red += pageContribution(page, 'Red') + white;
    green += pageContribution(page, 'Green') + white;
    blue += pageContribution(page, 'Blue') + white;
  }
  return {
    red: Math.min(4, Math.max(1, red)),
    green: Math.min(4, Math.max(1, green)),
    blue: Math.min(4, Math.max(1, blue)),
  };
}

export function applyLightToRgb(
  rgb: readonly [number, number, number],
  gains: LightGains,
  displayChannel: DisplayChannel = 'RGB',
): [number, number, number] {
  const composed: [number, number, number] = [
    Math.min(255, Math.max(0, Math.round(rgb[0] * gains.red))),
    Math.min(255, Math.max(0, Math.round(rgb[1] * gains.green))),
    Math.min(255, Math.max(0, Math.round(rgb[2] * gains.blue))),
  ];
  if (displayChannel === 'RGB') return composed;
  const value = composed[displayChannel === 'Red' ? 0 : displayChannel === 'Green' ? 1 : 2];
  return [value, value, value];
}

export function effectiveLumaGain(gains: LightGains, displayChannel: DisplayChannel = 'RGB'): number {
  if (displayChannel === 'Red') return gains.red;
  if (displayChannel === 'Green') return gains.green;
  if (displayChannel === 'Blue') return gains.blue;
  return 0.299 * gains.red + 0.587 * gains.green + 0.114 * gains.blue;
}

export function applyLightToGvStats(
  stats: GvStatsLike,
  gains: LightGains,
  displayChannel: DisplayChannel = 'RGB',
): GvStatsLike & { approximate: boolean } {
  const counts = stats.histogram;
  if (counts?.length === 256 && stats.pixels > 0 &&
      counts.every((count) => Number.isSafeInteger(count) && count >= 0) &&
      counts.reduce((sum, count) => sum + count, 0) === stats.pixels) {
    let sum = 0;
    let sumSq = 0;
    let min = 255;
    let max = 0;
    for (let value = 0; value < counts.length; value++) {
      const count = counts[value];
      if (count === 0) continue;
      const rgb = applyLightToRgb([value, value, value], gains, displayChannel);
      const luma = displayChannel === 'RGB' ? 0.299 * rgb[0] + 0.587 * rgb[1] + 0.114 * rgb[2] : rgb[0];
      sum += luma * count;
      sumSq += luma * luma * count;
      min = Math.min(min, luma);
      max = Math.max(max, luma);
    }
    const mean = sum / stats.pixels;
    return { mean, std: Math.sqrt(Math.max(0, sumSq / stats.pixels - mean * mean)), min, max, pixels: stats.pixels, approximate: false };
  }
  // Older backends return moments alone. They cannot reconstruct saturation;
  // callers must label the composed result as an estimate until rebuilt.
  const gain = effectiveLumaGain(gains, displayChannel);
  return {
    mean: Math.min(255, Math.max(0, stats.mean * gain)),
    std: Math.max(0, stats.std * gain),
    min: Math.min(255, Math.max(0, Math.round(stats.min * gain))),
    max: Math.min(255, Math.max(0, Math.round(stats.max * gain))),
    pixels: stats.pixels,
    approximate: gains.red !== 1 || gains.green !== 1 || gains.blue !== 1,
  };
}

export function lightMatrixValues(gains: LightGains, displayChannel: DisplayChannel = 'RGB'): string {
  if (displayChannel !== 'RGB') {
    const row = displayChannel === 'Red' ? `${gains.red} 0 0 0 0` :
      displayChannel === 'Green' ? `0 ${gains.green} 0 0 0` : `0 0 ${gains.blue} 0 0`;
    return `${row} ${row} ${row} 0 0 0 1 0`;
  }
  return `${gains.red} 0 0 0 0 0 ${gains.green} 0 0 0 0 0 ${gains.blue} 0 0 0 0 0 1 0`;
}
````

## File: tauri-app/src/lib/roi-tools.ts
````typescript
/**
 * Model for the reusable ROI tool rail (RoiToolPalette.svelte) and its mapping
 * onto the drawing overlay (RoiOverlay.svelte).
 *
 * The palette is a dumb UI: it renders every button and enables only the ones
 * a host passes in. Hosts differ solely in which buttons they switch on, so the
 * same component serves TEACH, GV measurement, and future tools.
 */
import type { RoiShape } from './service';

/** Every button the palette can render. */
export type RoiPaletteTool =
  | 'pointer'
  | 'add-rect'
  | 'add-ellipse'
  | 'add-polygon'
  | 'delete-rect'
  | 'delete-ellipse'
  | 'delete-polygon'
  | 'delete-roi';

/** What the overlay should do while a palette button is active. `select` is
 * the neutral pointer; `erase` removes the shape under the cursor. */
export type RoiDrawTool = 'select' | 'rect' | 'ellipse' | 'polygon' | 'erase';

/** Upper half of the rail: shape buttons that ADD to the selection. */
export const ROI_PALETTE_ADD: readonly RoiPaletteTool[] = ['add-rect', 'add-ellipse', 'add-polygon'];

/** Lower half of the rail: shape buttons that REMOVE from the selection. */
export const ROI_PALETTE_DELETE: readonly RoiPaletteTool[] = ['delete-rect', 'delete-ellipse', 'delete-polygon'];

/** Short labels, also used as tooltips/aria labels by the palette. */
export const ROI_PALETTE_LABELS: Record<RoiPaletteTool, string> = {
  pointer: '选择器（指针）',
  'add-rect': '添加矩形选区',
  'add-ellipse': '添加椭圆选区',
  'add-polygon': '添加多边形选区（右键闭合并首尾相接）',
  'delete-rect': '删除矩形选取',
  'delete-ellipse': '删除椭圆选取',
  'delete-polygon': '删除多边形选取',
  'delete-roi': '删除用户 ROI 选框（右键一键清空）',
};

/** The shape a palette button draws, or null for pointer / delete-ROI. */
export function shapeForTool(tool: RoiPaletteTool): RoiShape | null {
  if (tool === 'add-rect' || tool === 'delete-rect') return 'rect';
  if (tool === 'add-ellipse' || tool === 'delete-ellipse') return 'ellipse';
  if (tool === 'add-polygon' || tool === 'delete-polygon') return 'polygon';
  return null;
}

/** Overlay mode for a palette button. The three delete-shape buttons all map
 * to `erase` (the overlay drops the shape under the cursor); delete-ROI is an
 * action handled by the host, not a draw mode. */
export function drawToolFor(tool: RoiPaletteTool | null): RoiDrawTool {
  switch (tool) {
    case 'add-rect':
      return 'rect';
    case 'add-ellipse':
      return 'ellipse';
    case 'add-polygon':
      return 'polygon';
    case 'delete-rect':
    case 'delete-ellipse':
    case 'delete-polygon':
      return 'erase';
    default:
      return 'select';
  }
}
````

## File: tauri-app/src/lib/theme.ts
````typescript
// Theme engine. The palette is applied as a generated <style> sheet on
// startup (main.ts, pre-mount) so the first frame already has the persisted
// theme. Live in-place swaps are unreliable in this WebView2 build (style
// recalculation is lazily per-element and leaves mixed palettes), so the
// toggle in App.svelte persists the choice and reloads the page instead.

export type Theme = 'dark' | 'light';

export const DARK_VARS: Record<string, string> = {
  '--bg-dark': '#2d2d30',
  '--bg-darker': '#222222',
  '--bg-deep': '#1e1e1e',
  '--bg-panel': '#252526',
  '--bg-header': '#333337',
  '--bg-input': '#1e1e1e',
  '--bg-elev': '#484848',
  '--tint-ok': '#2e3d56',
  '--tint-bad': '#4a2d2d',
  '--tint-info': '#2d2d3d',
  '--tint-warn': '#4a3200',
  '--tint-warn-text': '#ffd88a',
  '--text-main': '#d4d4d4',
  '--text-muted': '#808080',
  '--accent-blue': '#007acc',
  '--accent-blue-bright': '#0088cc',
  '--status-green': '#8cc63f',
  '--border-color': '#3f3f46',
  '--border-strong': '#111111',
  '--slider-track': '#3e3e42',
  '--slider-thumb': '#007acc',
  '--toggle-bg': '#555555',
  '--toggle-bg-on': '#007acc',
  '--scrollbar-thumb': '#424242',
  '--scrollbar-thumb-hover': '#4f4f4f',
  '--row-insp': '#00ff00',
  '--row-sub': '#ffff00',
};

export const LIGHT_VARS: Record<string, string> = {
  '--bg-dark': '#f3f3f3',
  '--bg-darker': '#e4e4e4',
  '--bg-deep': '#eaeaea',
  '--bg-panel': '#ffffff',
  '--bg-header': '#e8e8e8',
  '--bg-input': '#ffffff',
  '--bg-elev': '#dcdcdc',
  '--tint-ok': '#dcefe2',
  '--tint-bad': '#f4dede',
  '--tint-info': '#e6e4f4',
  '--tint-warn': '#f7ecd2',
  '--tint-warn-text': '#6b5310',
  '--text-main': '#1f1f1f',
  '--text-muted': '#616161',
  '--accent-blue': '#0067c4',
  '--accent-blue-bright': '#0067c4',
  '--status-green': '#5a9e0d',
  '--border-color': '#d4d4d4',
  '--border-strong': '#c0c0c0',
  '--slider-track': '#c8c8c8',
  '--slider-thumb': '#0067c4',
  '--toggle-bg': '#b5b5b5',
  '--toggle-bg-on': '#0067c4',
  '--scrollbar-thumb': '#c1c1c1',
  '--scrollbar-thumb-hover': '#a8a8a8',
  '--row-insp': '#0a8a0a',
  '--row-sub': '#a07c00',
};

let epoch = 0;

export function applyTheme(theme: Theme): void {
  document.body.dataset['theme'] = theme;
  // Full-sheet swap with the palette. This WebView2 build recalculates style
  // lazily per element, so a live in-place swap leaves mixed palettes behind;
  // the toggle therefore persists and reloads (see App.svelte) - a fresh page
  // with the palette applied pre-mount always renders correctly.
  const vars = theme === 'light' ? LIGHT_VARS : DARK_VARS;
  const css = ':root{' + Object.entries(vars).map(([k, v]) => `${k}:${v};`).join('') + '}';
  let styleEl = document.getElementById('afvi-theme-vars') as HTMLStyleElement | null;
  if (!styleEl) {
    styleEl = document.createElement('style');
    styleEl.id = 'afvi-theme-vars';
    document.head.appendChild(styleEl);
  }
  styleEl.textContent = css;
}

export function persistTheme(theme: Theme): void {
  try {
    localStorage.setItem('afvi-theme', theme);
  } catch {
    // persistence is best-effort
  }
}

export function initialTheme(): Theme {
  try {
    return localStorage.getItem('afvi-theme') === 'light' ? 'light' : 'dark';
  } catch {
    return 'dark';
  }
}
````

````toml
# Rust build acceleration for this crate.
# - sccache: caches compiled third-party deps across clean builds / branch switches
#   (install: scoop install sccache; stats: sccache --show-stats).
#   Workspace crates with incremental compilation are passed through uncached.
# - rust-lld: the LLVM linker bundled with the Rust toolchain. This is the MSVC
#   equivalent of the GNU-only "-fuse-ld=lld" (which link.exe would reject).
[build]
rustc-wrapper = "sccache"

[target.x86_64-pc-windows-msvc]
linker = "rust-lld"
````

## File: tauri-app/src-tauri/examples/align_overlay_check.rs
````rust
//! Renders the colored Align/ROI overlay from the real layer tifs in
//! `tools/real_masks/` (see `Plan/ALIGN_OVERLAY_DEV_NOTES.md` for the full
//! method) and saves the full composite plus fiducial/BGA zoom crops for the
//! eyeball check. The pipeline itself lives in `align::overlay` - this example
//! is just the harness that re-tunes its display parameters on real data.
//!
//!   cargo run --release --example align_overlay_check

use image::imageops;

const REAL_DIR: &str = r"C:\develop\DMT_AFVI_Color_Parameter_AutoParse\tools\real_masks";
const OUT_DIR: &str = r"C:\develop\DMT_AFVI_Color_Parameter_AutoParse\Plan";

fn main() {
    let sr = image::open(std::path::Path::new(REAL_DIR).join("UNIT_0.tif"))
        .expect("UNIT_0.tif")
        .to_luma8();
    let metal = image::open(std::path::Path::new(REAL_DIR).join("Pattern.tif"))
        .expect("Pattern.tif")
        .to_luma8();
    println!("sr {}x{}, metal {}x{}", sr.width(), sr.height(), metal.width(), metal.height());

    // Candidates for the display compensation (working-grid px at 4096).
    // x compensation is the etch-shrink fix the user flagged ("横向太短");
    // y stays minimal.
    for dilate_x in [2u32, 4u32, 6u32] {
        let out = afvi_parse_lib::align::overlay::compose_overlay_with(&sr, &metal, 4096, dilate_x, 1)
            .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("compose failed: {error}"));
        let out_path = std::path::Path::new(OUT_DIR).join(format!("align_overlay_demo_dx{dilate_x}.png"));
        out.save(&out_path).expect("save demo");
        println!("dilate x{dilate_x}/y1: {}x{} -> {}", out.width(), out.height(), out_path.display());

        // 2x zoom on the BGA band to judge edge alignment and trace width.
        let zoom = imageops::crop_imm(&out, 819, 1053, 1405, 702).to_image();
        imageops::resize(&zoom, 1405, 702, imageops::FilterType::Nearest)
            .save(std::path::Path::new(OUT_DIR).join(format!("debug_zoom_dx{dilate_x}.png")))
            .ok();
    }

    // 2x zoom on the top-left fiducial cross (the registration anchor).
    let full = image::open(std::path::Path::new(OUT_DIR).join("align_overlay_demo_dx4.png")).expect("demo");
    let corner = imageops::crop_imm(&full, 0, 0, 468, 468).to_image();
    imageops::resize(&corner, 936, 936, imageops::FilterType::Nearest)
        .save(std::path::Path::new(OUT_DIR).join("debug_corner_dx4.png"))
        .ok();
    println!("wrote zooms to {OUT_DIR}");
}
````

## File: tauri-app/src-tauri/examples/aligndata_check.rs
````rust
//! One-off verification: can the `AlignData` trio (Metal/Open/SR) compose the
//! Align/ROI overlay? Prints layer metadata, then runs the real
//! `align::overlay::compose_overlay` pipeline on the pairs and saves the
//! composites for the eyeball check.
//!
//!   cargo run --release --example aligndata_check

use image::imageops;

const DIR: &str = r"C:\develop\DMT_AFVI_Color_Parameter_AutoParse\tools\aligndata_7M99-631";
const OUT_DIR: &str = r"C:\develop\DMT_AFVI_Color_Parameter_AutoParse\Plan";

fn report(name: &str) -> image::GrayImage {
    let path = std::path::Path::new(DIR).join(format!("{name}.tif"));
    let img = image::open(&path).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{name}: {e}"));
    println!(
        "{name}: {}x{} color={:?}",
        img.width(),
        img.height(),
        img.color()
    );
    let luma = img.to_luma8();
    let white = luma.pixels().filter(|p| p.0[0] >= 128).count();
    println!("{name}: white {:.2}%", 100.0 * white as f64 / luma.pixels().len() as f64);
    luma
}

fn try_compose(tag: &str, sr: &image::GrayImage, metal: &image::GrayImage) {
    match afvi_parse_lib::align::overlay::compose_overlay(sr, metal) {
        Ok(out) => {
            let path = std::path::Path::new(OUT_DIR).join(format!("aligndata_overlay_{tag}.png"));
            out.save(&path).expect("save");
            println!(
                "compose {tag}: OK {}x{} -> {}",
                out.width(),
                out.height(),
                path.display()
            );
            // 2x zoom on the top-left fiducial (registration anchor).
            let corner = imageops::crop_imm(&out, 0, 0, 468, 468).to_image();
            imageops::resize(&corner, 936, 936, imageops::FilterType::Nearest)
                .save(std::path::Path::new(OUT_DIR).join(format!("aligndata_corner_{tag}.png")))
                .ok();
        }
        Err(error) => println!("compose {tag}: FAILED - {error}"),
    }
}

fn main() {
    let metal = report("Metal");
    let open = report("Open");
    let sr = report("SR");
    try_compose("sr_metal", &sr, &metal);
    try_compose("sr_open", &sr, &open);
    try_compose("metal_open", &metal, &open);
}
````

## File: tauri-app/src-tauri/examples/aligndata_identity.rs
````rust
//! Diagnostic: are the AlignData layers pre-registered on one shared grid?
//! Composes SR+Metal with NO cross-layer registration (identity on the union
//! bbox) and prints each layer's white bbox, to compare against the real
//! machine's overlay screenshot.
//!
//!   cargo run --release --example aligndata_identity

use image::{imageops, GrayImage, Luma, Rgba, RgbaImage};

const DIR: &str = r"C:\develop\DMT_AFVI_Color_Parameter_AutoParse\tools\aligndata_7M99-631";
const OUT: &str = r"C:\develop\DMT_AFVI_Color_Parameter_AutoParse\Plan\aligndata_identity.png";

fn load(name: &str) -> (GrayImage, (u32, u32, u32, u32)) {
    let luma = image::open(std::path::Path::new(DIR).join(format!("{name}.tif")))
        .expect(name)
        .to_luma8();
    let (mut x0, mut y0, mut x1, mut y1) = (u32::MAX, u32::MAX, 0u32, 0u32);
    for (x, y, p) in luma.enumerate_pixels() {
        if p.0[0] >= 128 {
            x0 = x0.min(x);
            y0 = y0.min(y);
            x1 = x1.max(x);
            y1 = y1.max(y);
        }
    }
    println!("{name}: {}x{} white bbox=({x0},{y0})-({x1},{y1})", luma.width(), luma.height());
    (luma, (x0, y0, x1, y1))
}

fn main() {
    let (sr, sb) = load("SR");
    let (metal, mb) = load("Metal");

    let x0 = sb.0.min(mb.0);
    let y0 = sb.1.min(mb.1);
    let x1 = sb.2.max(mb.2);
    let y1 = sb.3.max(mb.3);
    let (w, h) = (x1 - x0 + 1, y1 - y0 + 1);
    println!("union bbox {w}x{h}");

    let crop = |img: &GrayImage, b: (u32, u32, u32, u32)| -> GrayImage {
        imageops::crop_imm(img, b.0, b.1, b.2 - b.0 + 1, b.3 - b.1 + 1).to_image()
    };
    let sr_c = crop(&sr, (x0, y0, x1, y1));
    let metal_c = crop(&metal, (x0, y0, x1, y1));

    let work_w = 2000;
    let work_h = (h as f64 / w as f64 * work_w as f64).round() as u32;
    let sr_s = imageops::resize(&sr_c, work_w, work_h, imageops::FilterType::Triangle);
    let metal_s = imageops::resize(&metal_c, work_w, work_h, imageops::FilterType::Triangle);
    let _ = Luma([0u8]);

    let mut out = RgbaImage::from_pixel(work_w, work_h, Rgba([0, 0, 0, 255]));
    for (x, y, p) in sr_s.enumerate_pixels() {
        if p.0[0] >= 128 {
            out.put_pixel(x, y, Rgba([26, 158, 40, 255]));
        }
    }
    for (x, y, p) in metal_s.enumerate_pixels() {
        if p.0[0] >= 128 {
            out.put_pixel(x, y, Rgba([255, 214, 0, 255]));
        }
    }
    let _ = Luma([0u8]);
    out.save(OUT).expect("save");
    println!("wrote {OUT}");
}
````

## File: tauri-app/src-tauri/examples/aligndata_resolve_check.rs
````rust
//! Real-data verification of the Plan 07 resolver chain against the live
//! shares: PxRepository model dir root > PxRepository\AlignData >
//! PxInventory\INSPECT_SPEC\<model>-00\AlignData > safe Missing, plus one
//! end-to-end identity compose from the resolved 25fbo015-15 trio.
//!
//!   cargo run --release --example aligndata_resolve_check

use afvi_parse_lib::align::{resolve_aligndata_tifs, AlignDataLookup};

const REPO: &str = r"\\192.168.1.61\PxRepository";
const INVENTORY: &str = r"\\192.168.1.61\PxInventory";
const OUT: &str = r"C:\develop\DMT_AFVI_Color_Parameter_AutoParse\Plan\aligndata_25fbo015_overlay.png";

fn probe(tag: &str, repo: &str, inventory: Option<&str>, model: &str) -> Option<std::sync::Arc<afvi_parse_lib::align::AlignDataLayers>> {
    match resolve_aligndata_tifs(repo, inventory, model) {
        Ok(AlignDataLookup::Found(layers)) => {
            println!("{tag}: FOUND source={} open={}", layers.source, layers.open.is_some());
            println!("  metal {}", layers.metal.display());
            Some(std::sync::Arc::new(*layers))
        }
        Ok(AlignDataLookup::Missing { searched }) => {
            println!("{tag}: MISSING (safe empty state), probed {} location(s):", searched.len());
            for s in &searched {
                println!("  - {s}");
            }
            None
        }
        Err(error) => {
            println!("{tag}: HARD ERROR - {error}");
            None
        }
    }
}

fn main() {
    // 1. newest drop layout: trio directly in the PxRepository model dir
    let _ = probe("repo-root 25fbo015-15", REPO, Some(INVENTORY), "25fbo015-15");
    // 2. trio in the model's AlignData subfolder (7M99-631 layout)
    let _ = probe("repo-sub 7M99-631   ", REPO, Some(INVENTORY), "7M99-631");
    // 2b. trio at the INSPECT_SPEC dir root next to its AlignData folder -
    //     the shallow root pair must win the breadth-first scan
    let empty_repo = std::env::temp_dir().join("afvi_resolve_check_empty");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&empty_repo).unwrap();
    let _ = probe("inv-root  7M99-631   ", empty_repo.to_str().unwrap(), Some(INVENTORY), "7M99-631");
    // 3. model without the trio anywhere -> safe Missing, never an error
    let _ = probe("none      danny      ", REPO, Some(INVENTORY), "danny");
    // 4. repository without the model + real inventory -> inventory wins
    let _ = probe("inv-only  25fbo015-15", empty_repo.to_str().unwrap(), Some(INVENTORY), "25fbo015-15");

    // 5. end-to-end: identity compose from the resolved trio (real 23 MB tifs)
    if let Some(layers) = probe("compose   25fbo015-15", REPO, Some(INVENTORY), "25fbo015-15") {
        let started = std::time::Instant::now();
        let metal = image::open(&layers.metal).expect("metal").to_luma8();
        let sr = image::open(&layers.sr).expect("sr").to_luma8();
        println!("  decoded {}x{} + {}x{} in {:?}", metal.width(), metal.height(), sr.width(), sr.height(), started.elapsed());
        let composite = afvi_parse_lib::align::overlay::compose_identity(&sr, &metal, 4096).expect("compose");
        composite.save(OUT).expect("save");
        println!("  composed {}x{} -> {OUT}", composite.width(), composite.height());
    }
}
````

## File: tauri-app/src-tauri/examples/inspect_masks.rs
````rust
//! Inspect the real masks: render downscaled grayscale previews and print
//! level statistics to pin down each layer's polarity (white-on-black vs
//! black-on-white).
//!
//!   cargo run --release --example inspect_masks

use image::imageops;

fn main() {
    for name in ["UNIT_0.tif", "Pattern.tif"] {
        let path = std::path::Path::new(r"C:\develop\DMT_AFVI_Color_Parameter_AutoParse\tools\real_masks").join(name);
        let img = image::open(&path).expect(name).to_luma8();
        let n = (img.width() as u64) * (img.height() as u64);
        let mut hist = [0u64; 8];
        for l in img.pixels() {
            hist[(l.0[0] / 32) as usize] += 1;
        }
        let buckets: Vec<String> = hist
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .map(|(i, c)| format!("{:0>3}-{:<3}:{:5.1}%", i * 32, i * 32 + 31, *c as f64 / n as f64 * 100.0))
            .collect();
        println!("{name}: {}x{}, levels {}", img.width(), img.height(), buckets.join("  "));

        let small = imageops::resize(&img, 1400, (img.height() as f64 / img.width() as f64 * 1400.0) as u32, imageops::FilterType::Triangle);
        let out = format!(r"C:\develop\DMT_AFVI_Color_Parameter_AutoParse\Plan\debug_real_{}", name.replace(".tif", ".png"));
        small.save(&out).unwrap();
        println!("  wrote {out}");
    }
}
````

## File: tauri-app/src-tauri/examples/metal_sim_check.rs
````rust
//! Real-data check for the ROI-driven align simulation (Plan 07 C): seed a
//! misalignment on the 25fbo015-15 pair, then run the REAL M5 ROI pipeline
//! (verify_with_rois) with (a) auto-picked feature-rich boxes - must align,
//! and (b) deliberately featureless boxes - must fail the verdict.
//!
//!   cargo run --release --example metal_sim_check

use afvi_parse_lib::align::ecc::Transform;
use afvi_parse_lib::align::fiducial::{verify_with_rois, RoiRectIn};
use afvi_parse_lib::align::metal_sim::{invert, offset_from_seed, sim_config, warp_layer};
use afvi_parse_lib::align::overlay::compose_median_metal;
use image::{GrayImage, GenericImageView};

const MEDIAN: &str = r"\\192.168.1.61\PxRepository\25fbo015-15\2.0\Line\Top\Layer\MEDIAN\Median_0_1_0.tif";
const REPO: &str = r"\\192.168.1.61\PxRepository";
const INVENTORY: &str = r"\\192.168.1.61\PxInventory";
const OUT_DIR: &str = r"C:\develop\DMT_AFVI_Color_Parameter_AutoParse\Plan";
const GRID_MAX: u32 = 3072;
const BOX: f64 = 180.0;
const SEED: u64 = 42;

fn to_grid(img: GrayImage) -> GrayImage {
    let (w, h) = img.dimensions();
    if w.max(h) <= GRID_MAX {
        return img;
    }
    let scale = GRID_MAX as f64 / w.max(h) as f64;
    image::imageops::resize(
        &img,
        (w as f64 * scale).round() as u32,
        (h as f64 * scale).round() as u32,
        image::imageops::FilterType::Triangle,
    )
}

/// The brightest / dimmest BOX-sized window per quadrant: brightest = marks
/// (feature-rich, what a user SHOULD draw), dimmest = blank board (the trap).
fn pick_windows(displaced: &GrayImage, brightest: bool) -> Vec<RoiRectIn> {
    let (w, h) = (displaced.width() as i64, displaced.height() as i64);
    let (bw, bh) = (BOX as i64, BOX as i64);
    let quads = [
        (0i64, 0i64, w / 2, h / 2),
        (w / 2, 0, w - bw, h / 2),
        (0, h / 2, w / 2, h - bh),
        (w / 2, h / 2, w - bw, h - bh),
    ];
    let mut rois = Vec::new();
    for (qi, (x0, y0, x1, y1)) in quads.iter().enumerate() {
        let mut best: Option<(f64, i64, i64)> = None;
        let mut y = *y0;
        while y + bh <= *y1 {
            let mut x = *x0;
            while x + bw <= *x1 {
                let mut sum = 0.0f64;
                for yy in (y..y + bh).step_by(4) {
                    for xx in (x..x + bw).step_by(4) {
                        sum += f64::from(displaced.get_pixel(xx as u32, yy as u32).0[0]);
                    }
                }
                let better = match best {
                    None => true,
                    Some((best_sum, _, _)) => if brightest { sum > best_sum } else { sum < best_sum },
                };
                if better {
                    best = Some((sum, x, y));
                }
                x += 40;
            }
            y += 40;
        }
        let (_, x, y) = best.expect("quadrant non-empty");
        rois.push(RoiRectIn {
            name: format!("ROI-{}", qi + 1),
            x: x as f64,
            y: y as f64,
            w: BOX,
            h: BOX,
        });
    }
    rois
}

fn main() {
    let started = std::time::Instant::now();
    let median = to_grid(image::open(std::path::Path::new(MEDIAN)).expect("median").to_luma8());
    let metal = match afvi_parse_lib::align::resolve_aligndata_tifs(REPO, Some(INVENTORY), "25fbo015-15") {
        Ok(afvi_parse_lib::align::AlignDataLookup::Found(layers)) => {
            to_grid(image::open(&layers.metal).expect("metal").to_luma8())
        }
        _ => panic!("no AlignData trio"),
    };
    println!("grid {}x{} ({:?})", median.width(), median.height(), started.elapsed());

    let offset = offset_from_seed(SEED, median.width(), median.height());
    println!("simulated offset tx={:.1} ty={:.1} theta={:.3}deg", offset.tx, offset.ty, offset.theta_deg);
    let truth = invert(&offset); // what the fit should recover
    println!("expected fit    tx={:.1} ty={:.1} theta={:.3}deg", truth.tx, truth.ty, truth.theta_deg);
    let displaced = warp_layer(&metal, &offset);
    compose_median_metal(&median, &displaced, GRID_MAX)
        .unwrap()
        .save(std::path::Path::new(OUT_DIR).join("metal_sim_offset.png"))
        .unwrap();

    for (tag, brightest) in [("good-ROIs", true), ("bad-ROIs", false)] {
        let rois = pick_windows(&displaced, brightest);
        for r in &rois {
            print!("  {} ({},{},{},{}) ", r.name, r.x, r.y, r.w, r.h);
        }
        println!();
        let report = verify_with_rois(&displaced, &median, &rois, &sim_config(), Transform::default()).expect("verify");
        println!(
            "{tag}: verdict={} inliers={}/{} mean_ncc={:.3} resid_rms={:.2} fit tx={:.1} ty={:.1} theta={:.3} ({:?})",
            report.verdict.level,
            report.inliers,
            report.matches.len(),
            report.mean_ncc,
            report.residual_rms,
            report.fit.tx,
            report.fit.ty,
            report.fit.theta_deg,
            report.verdict.reasons
        );
        let corrected = warp_layer(&displaced, &report.fit);
        compose_median_metal(&median, &corrected, GRID_MAX)
            .unwrap()
            .save(std::path::Path::new(OUT_DIR).join(format!("metal_sim_{tag}.png")))
            .unwrap();
    }
    println!("done ({:?})", started.elapsed());
}
````

## File: tauri-app/src-tauri/examples/metal_sim_debug.rs
````rust
//! Diagnose the user's failed 5-box align (seed 6320): four boxes on the
//! corner fiducial crosses + one on a scan-only white mark. Prints per-box
//! NCC/located/residual so the failure mode is a number, not a guess.
//!
//!   cargo run --release --example metal_sim_debug

use afvi_parse_lib::align::ecc::Transform;
use afvi_parse_lib::align::fiducial::{verify_with_rois, FiducialConfig, RoiRectIn};
use afvi_parse_lib::align::metal_sim::{offset_from_seed, sim_config, warp_layer};
use image::GenericImageView;

const MEDIAN: &str = r"\\192.168.1.61\PxRepository\25fbo015-15\2.0\Line\Top\Layer\MEDIAN\Median_0_1_0.tif";
const REPO: &str = r"\\192.168.1.61\PxRepository";
const INVENTORY: &str = r"\\192.168.1.61\PxInventory";
const GRID_MAX: u32 = 3072;
const SEED: u64 = 6320;
/// Half-side of the boxes the "user" draws (300 px total, like the app).
const BOX: f64 = 150.0;

fn to_grid(img: image::GrayImage) -> image::GrayImage {
    let (w, h) = img.dimensions();
    let long = w.max(h);
    if long <= GRID_MAX {
        return img;
    }
    let scale = GRID_MAX as f64 / long as f64;
    image::imageops::resize(
        &img,
        (w as f64 * scale).round() as u32,
        (h as f64 * scale).round() as u32,
        image::imageops::FilterType::Triangle,
    )
}

/// Per-box patch stats on the displaced metal layer: white ratio + std,
/// so "featureless box" is visible before any NCC runs.
fn patch_stats(layer: &image::GrayImage, roi: &RoiRectIn) -> (f64, f64) {
    let (x0, y0) = (roi.x.max(0.0) as u32, roi.y.max(0.0) as u32);
    let x1 = (roi.x + roi.w).min(f64::from(layer.width())).max(0.0) as u32;
    let y1 = (roi.y + roi.h).min(f64::from(layer.height())).max(0.0) as u32;
    if x1 <= x0 || y1 <= y0 {
        return (0.0, 0.0);
    }
    let mut sum = 0.0;
    let mut sum_sq = 0.0;
    let mut white = 0u32;
    let mut n = 0u32;
    for y in y0..y1 {
        for x in x0..x1 {
            let v = f64::from(layer.get_pixel(x, y).0[0]);
            sum += v;
            sum_sq += v * v;
            if v >= 128.0 {
                white += 1;
            }
            n += 1;
        }
    }
    let mean = sum / f64::from(n);
    ((100 * white) as f64 / f64::from(n), (sum_sq / f64::from(n) - mean * mean).sqrt())
}

fn main() {
    let median = to_grid(image::open(std::path::Path::new(MEDIAN)).expect("median").to_luma8());
    let metal = match afvi_parse_lib::align::resolve_aligndata_tifs(REPO, Some(INVENTORY), "25fbo015-15") {
        Ok(afvi_parse_lib::align::AlignDataLookup::Found(layers)) => to_grid(image::open(&layers.metal).expect("metal").to_luma8()),
        _ => panic!("no trio"),
    };
    let offset = offset_from_seed(SEED, median.width(), median.height());
    println!("offset tx={:.1} ty={:.1} theta={:.3}", offset.tx, offset.ty, offset.theta_deg);
    let displaced = warp_layer(&metal, &offset);

    // approximated from the user's screenshot (grid px, 3072x2107)
    let rois = vec![
        RoiRectIn { name: "ROI-2-TLcross".into(), x: 22.0, y: 0.0, w: 143.0, h: 140.0 },
        RoiRectIn { name: "ROI-3-BLcross".into(), x: 16.0, y: 1992.0, w: 140.0, h: 155.0 },
        RoiRectIn { name: "ROI-4-BRcross".into(), x: 2836.0, y: 1960.0, w: 149.0, h: 171.0 },
        RoiRectIn { name: "ROI-5-whitemark".into(), x: 2623.0, y: 594.0, w: 146.0, h: 177.0 },
        RoiRectIn { name: "ROI-6-pad".into(), x: 1240.0, y: 840.0, w: 180.0, h: 180.0 },
    ];
    for roi in &rois {
        let (white, std) = patch_stats(&displaced, roi);
        println!("{:>16}: white {white:5.1}%  std {std:6.1}", roi.name);
    }

    // the shipped config on the approximated boxes, then the honest sweep:
    // each seed's boxes are placed on the features AS SEEN AT THAT SEED'S
    // offset (what a user drawing on the view actually does)
    let config = sim_config();
    let report = verify_with_rois(&displaced, &median, &rois, &config, Transform::default()).expect("verify");
    println!("== seed {SEED}: verdict={} inliers={}/{}", report.verdict.level, report.inliers, report.matches.len());

    // nominal (undisplaced) positions of four corner crosses + one pad,
    // detected from the original metal layer: brightest white cluster within
    // each corner region
    let nominal = cross_nominals(&metal);
    println!("nominal crosses: {:?}", nominal);

    let mut failed = 0usize;
    let mut worst_located = 5usize;
    for seed in 0..400u64 {
        let seed = seed * 7919 + 13;
        let offset = offset_from_seed(seed, median.width(), median.height());
        let displaced = warp_layer(&metal, &offset);
        let placed: Vec<RoiRectIn> = nominal
            .iter()
            .chain(std::iter::once(&(1240.0 + 90.0, 840.0 + 90.0)))
            .enumerate()
            .map(|(i, (cx, cy))| RoiRectIn {
                name: format!("ROI-{i}"),
                x: cx + offset.tx - BOX,
                y: cy + offset.ty - BOX,
                w: BOX * 2.0,
                h: BOX * 2.0,
            })
            .collect();
        let r = verify_with_rois(&displaced, &median, &placed, &config, Transform::default()).unwrap();
        let located = r.matches.iter().filter(|m| m.located).count();
        worst_located = worst_located.min(located);
        if r.verdict.level != "ok" {
            failed += 1;
            if failed <= 5 {
                println!(
                    "  FAIL seed {:>8}: tx={:+6.1} ty={:+6.1} located={located} verdict={} {}",
                    seed,
                    offset.tx,
                    offset.ty,
                    r.verdict.level,
                    r.verdict.reasons.join(" | ")
                );
            }
        }
    }
    println!("honest sweep: {failed}/400 verdicts not-ok; worst located={worst_located}/5");
}

/// Centroid of the white blob nearest each canvas corner (within 400 px) on
/// the ORIGINAL metal layer - the four corner fiducial crosses.
fn cross_nominals(metal: &image::GrayImage) -> Vec<(f64, f64)> {
    let (w, h) = (metal.width() as i64, metal.height() as i64);
    let corners = [(0i64, 0i64), (0, h - 1), (w - 1, h - 1), (w - 1, 0)];
    corners
        .iter()
        .map(|(cx, cy)| {
            let (mut sx, mut sy, mut n) = (0f64, 0f64, 0u32);
            for y in (cy - 400).max(0)..=(cy + 400).min(h - 1) {
                for x in (cx - 400).max(0)..=(cx + 400).min(w - 1) {
                    if metal.get_pixel(x as u32, y as u32).0[0] >= 128 {
                        sx += x as f64;
                        sy += y as f64;
                        n += 1;
                    }
                }
            }
            (sx / f64::from(n), sy / f64::from(n))
        })
        .collect()
}
````

## File: tauri-app/src-tauri/src/align/generator.rs
````rust
//! M1 synthetic case generator (Plan 05): ground-truth injection.
//!
//! Given an ideal base image plus `(seed, truth, params)` it produces the
//! teaching triple `(template, input, truth)`:
//!
//! 1. `template` = the base image downsampled to the case's working grid;
//! 2. `input`    = the template warped by the known truth transform, then
//!    degraded by illumination / blur / noise / occlusion.
//!
//! Every random decision draws from [`SeededRng`], never a global RNG, so the
//! same seed + params + truth regenerate the exact same bytes (D4). The RNG,
//! the warp and the degradation order are deliberately hand-rolled and kept
//! small: they are teaching material for M4's step-through view.

use super::{AlignCase, CaseParams, TruthTransform};
use image::{GrayImage, Luma};
use std::fs;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

// ---- seeded RNG: splitmix64 seeding + xoshiro256** + Box-Muller gaussian ----

/// Deterministic PRNG owned by one case generation. Hand-rolled so that the
/// byte-level reproducibility contract never depends on a third-party crate's
/// version bump changing its stream.
pub struct SeededRng {
    state: [u64; 4],
    /// Box-Muller produces gaussians in pairs; the spare one is kept here.
    spare: Option<f64>,
}

impl SeededRng {
    pub fn new(seed: u64) -> Self {
        // splitmix64 expands one seed into the 256-bit xoshiro state.
        let mut mix = seed;
        let mut next = || {
            mix = mix.wrapping_add(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);
            let mut z = mix;
            z = (z ^ (z >> 30)).wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
            z = (z ^ (z >> 27)).wrapping_mul(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB);
            z ^ (z >> 31)
        };
        Self { state: [next(), next(), next(), next()], spare: None }
    }

    fn next_u64(&mut self) -> u64 {
        let result = self.state[1].wrapping_mul(5).rotate_left(7).wrapping_mul(9);
        let t = self.state[1] << 17;
        self.state[2] ^= self.state[0];
        self.state[3] ^= self.state[1];
        self.state[1] ^= self.state[2];
        self.state[0] ^= self.state[3];
        self.state[2] ^= t;
        self.state[3] = self.state[3].rotate_left(45);
        result
    }

    /// Uniform in `[0, 1)`.
    pub fn next_f64(&mut self) -> f64 {
        // 53 random mantissa bits: uniform over the doubles in [0,1).
        (self.next_u64() >> 11) as f64 * (1.0 / (1u64 << 53) as f64)
    }

    /// Uniform in `[low, high)`.
    pub fn range_f64(&mut self, low: f64, high: f64) -> f64 {
        low + self.next_f64() * (high - low)
    }

    /// Standard normal via Box-Muller. `sin`/`cos`/`ln` come from the platform
    /// libm, so byte identity holds per platform build (the classroom fleet is
    /// one Windows x64 build) rather than across all architectures.
    pub fn gaussian(&mut self) -> f64 {
        if let Some(spare) = self.spare.take() {
            return spare;
        }
        let u1 = self.next_f64().max(f64::MIN_POSITIVE); // ln(0) guard
        let u2 = self.next_f64();
        let r = (-2.0 * u1.ln()).sqrt();
        let theta = std::f64::consts::TAU * u2;
        self.spare = Some(r * theta.sin());
        r * theta.cos()
    }
}

// ---- geometry: inverse warp with bilinear sampling ----

/// Applies `truth` to `template` and returns the warped image: for each output
/// pixel the *inverse* transform is sampled from the template (bilinear,
/// border = black). The transform maps template -> input as
/// `q = c + R(θ)·(s·(p − c)) + t` with `c` the working-grid center, so a
/// truth of `(0, 0, 0°, 1.0)` reproduces the template exactly.
///
/// Content near the borders rotates out of the canvas and is clipped - the
/// aligners see the same canvas size on both sides, which is what M2's phase
/// correlation needs.
pub fn warp_transform(template: &GrayImage, truth: &TruthTransform) -> GrayImage {
    let (width, height) = template.dimensions();
    let (cx, cy) = (f64::from(width - 1) / 2.0, f64::from(height - 1) / 2.0);
    let theta = truth.theta_deg.to_radians();
    let (cos, sin) = (theta.cos(), theta.sin());
    let scale = truth.scale;
    let (tx, ty) = (truth.tx_px, truth.ty_px);
    // Inverse of the forward transform: p = c + R(-θ)·((q − c − t) / s).
    let inverse = move |qx: f64, qy: f64| -> (f64, f64) {
        let dx = (qx - cx - tx) / scale;
        let dy = (qy - cy - ty) / scale;
        (cx + dx * cos + dy * sin, cy - dx * sin + dy * cos)
    };

    let mut out = GrayImage::new(width, height);
    for y in 0..height {
        for x in 0..width {
            let (sx, sy) = inverse(f64::from(x), f64::from(y));
            let value = sample_bilinear(template, sx, sy).unwrap_or(0);
            out.put_pixel(x, y, Luma([value]));
        }
    }
    out
}

fn sample_bilinear(image: &GrayImage, x: f64, y: f64) -> Option<u8> {
    let (w, h) = image.dimensions();
    if x < 0.0 || y < 0.0 || x > f64::from(w - 1) || y > f64::from(h - 1) {
        return None;
    }
    let x0 = x.floor() as u32;
    let y0 = y.floor() as u32;
    let x1 = (x0 + 1).min(w - 1);
    let y1 = (y0 + 1).min(h - 1);
    let (fx, fy) = (x - f64::from(x0), y - f64::from(y0));
    let get = |px: u32, py: u32| -> f64 { f64::from(image.get_pixel(px, py).0[0]) };
    let top = get(x0, y0) * (1.0 - fx) + get(x1, y0) * fx;
    let bottom = get(x0, y1) * (1.0 - fx) + get(x1, y1) * fx;
    Some((top * (1.0 - fy) + bottom * fy).round().clamp(0.0, 255.0) as u8)
}

// ---- degradation chain (fixed order: illumination -> blur -> noise -> occlusion) ----

/// Downsamples `base` to the case working grid by the integer factor
/// `params.downsample` (area-average via `thumbnail`). This becomes the
/// template; the truth transform is expressed in these working-grid px.
pub fn make_template(base: &GrayImage, params: &CaseParams) -> GrayImage {
    if params.downsample <= 1 {
        return base.clone();
    }
    let factor = f64::from(params.downsample);
    let (w, h) = base.dimensions();
    // Round-to-zero keeps the factor an exact divisor semantics; at least 1px.
    let dw = (w as f64 / factor).max(1.0) as u32;
    let dh = (h as f64 / factor).max(1.0) as u32;
    image::imageops::resize(base, dw, dh, image::imageops::FilterType::Triangle)
}

/// Renders the input image: template + warp + degradations, in the fixed
/// contract order documented on the module. `rng` must be the case's own
/// [`SeededRng`]; nothing here reads global entropy.
pub fn render_input(template: &GrayImage, rng: &mut SeededRng, truth: &TruthTransform, params: &CaseParams) -> GrayImage {
    let warped = warp_transform(template, truth);

    // 1. illumination: gain then offset, clamped per pixel.
    let mut input = if params.gain != 1.0 || params.offset != 0.0 {
        let mut lit = warped.clone();
        for pixel in lit.pixels_mut() {
            let v = f64::from(pixel.0[0]) * params.gain + params.offset;
            pixel.0[0] = v.round().clamp(0.0, 255.0) as u8;
        }
        lit
    } else {
        warped
    };

    // 2. blur.
    if params.blur_sigma > 0.0 {
        input = imageproc::filter::gaussian_blur_f32(&input, params.blur_sigma as f32);
    }

    // 3. noise.
    if params.noise_sigma > 0.0 {
        for pixel in input.pixels_mut() {
            let v = f64::from(pixel.0[0]) + rng.gaussian() * params.noise_sigma;
            pixel.0[0] = v.round().clamp(0.0, 255.0) as u8;
        }
    }

    // 4. occlusion: one black rectangle covering ~occlusion_ratio of the
    //    canvas, placed by the RNG (the classic "坏板/遮挡" failure mode).
    if params.occlusion_ratio > 0.0 {
        let (w, h) = input.dimensions();
        let ratio = params.occlusion_ratio.min(1.0);
        // Pick the rectangle shape first, then position it fully inside.
        let aspect = rng.range_f64(0.5, 2.0);
        let area = f64::from(w) * f64::from(h) * ratio;
        let rw = ((area * aspect).sqrt().round() as u32).clamp(1, w);
        let rh = ((area / aspect).sqrt().round() as u32).clamp(1, h);
        let rx = (rng.next_f64() * f64::from(w - rw + 1)) as u32;
        let ry = (rng.next_f64() * f64::from(h - rh + 1)) as u32;
        for y in ry..ry + rh {
            for x in rx..rx + rw {
                input.put_pixel(x, y, Luma([0]));
            }
        }
    }

    input
}

/// Truth ranges for cases where the caller does not pin the transform: the
/// generator derives it from the case RNG so that "case = seed + params"
/// still holds verbatim (D4). Modest by design - M2's phase correlation must
/// be able to solve them.
pub fn derive_truth(rng: &mut SeededRng, template: &GrayImage) -> TruthTransform {
    let (w, h) = template.dimensions();
    let drift = f64::from(w.min(h)) * 0.05; // up to 5% of the short side
    TruthTransform {
        tx_px: rng.range_f64(-drift, drift),
        ty_px: rng.range_f64(-drift, drift),
        theta_deg: rng.range_f64(-1.5, 1.5),
        scale: rng.range_f64(0.99, 1.01),
    }
}

/// The generated triple plus everything needed to persist it. `truth` is the
/// resolved transform - either the caller-pinned one or the derived one - so
/// the persisted case record always describes the input exactly.
pub struct GeneratedCase {
    pub template: GrayImage,
    pub input: GrayImage,
    pub truth: TruthTransform,
}

/// Full generation from a base image. `truth = None` derives it from the RNG
/// (see [`derive_truth`]); `Some(truth)` is the instructor-pinned mode.
pub fn generate_case(base: &GrayImage, seed: u64, truth: Option<TruthTransform>, params: &CaseParams) -> GeneratedCase {
    let template = make_template(base, params);
    let mut rng = SeededRng::new(seed);
    // IMPORTANT draw order: truth (if derived) is drawn BEFORE the noise so
    // that pinning a truth never shifts the degradation stream.
    let truth = truth.unwrap_or_else(|| derive_truth(&mut rng, &template));
    let input = render_input(&template, &mut rng, &truth, params);
    GeneratedCase { template, input, truth }
}

// ---- case library on disk ----

/// Case library root layout: `<root>/<case_id>/{case.json, template.png, input.png}`.
/// PNG (not JPEG) keeps the reproducibility contract byte-exact; previews for
/// the UI are encoded at IPC time, never stored.
pub const CASE_FILE: &str = "case.json";
pub const TEMPLATE_FILE: &str = "template.png";
pub const INPUT_FILE: &str = "input.png";

/// Case id from its identity triple. Same seed + model + side regenerates into
/// the same folder - regeneration is idempotent (the lesson plan can re-derive
/// a case at any time), different seeds never collide.
pub fn case_id(model_name: &str, side: &str, seed: u64) -> String {
    let safe_model: String = model_name
        .chars()
        .map(|c| if c.is_alphanumeric() || c == '-' || c == '_' { c } else { '_' })
        .collect();
    format!("{}_{}_{}", safe_model, side.to_ascii_uppercase(), seed)
}

/// Writes one case into the library and returns the case directory. The
/// `case.case_id` is authoritative; pass it already resolved via [`case_id`].
pub fn save_case(root: &Path, case: &AlignCase, template: &GrayImage, input: &GrayImage) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
    case.validate()?;
    let dir = root.join(&case.case_id);
    // Write-then-rename would be nicer, but a torn case.json is detected by
    // the reader (validate) and regeneration is idempotent, so plain writes
    // keep the library inspectable.
    fs::create_dir_all(&dir).map_err(|error| format!("Cannot create {}: {error}", dir.display()))?;
    let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(case).map_err(|error| format!("Cannot serialize the case: {error}"))?;
    fs::write(dir.join(CASE_FILE), json).map_err(|error| format!("Cannot write {CASE_FILE}: {error}"))?;
    write_png(&dir.join(TEMPLATE_FILE), template)?;
    write_png(&dir.join(INPUT_FILE), input)?;
    Ok(dir)
}

fn write_png(path: &Path, image: &GrayImage) -> Result<(), String> {
    image.save_with_format(path, image::ImageFormat::Png).map_err(|error| format!("Cannot write {}: {error}", path.display()))
}

/// Lists every valid case in the library, sorted by id. Broken or future-
/// schema folders are skipped (with a stderr note) instead of failing the
/// whole listing - the classroom must survive one damaged folder.
pub fn list_cases(root: &Path) -> Result<Vec<AlignCase>, String> {
    let mut cases = Vec::new();
    let entries = match fs::read_dir(root) {
        Ok(entries) => entries,
        // An absent library is an empty library, not an error.
        Err(_) => return Ok(cases),
    };
    for entry in entries.flatten() {
        let case_file = entry.path().join(CASE_FILE);
        if !case_file.is_file() {
            continue;
        }
        match fs::read_to_string(&case_file)
            .map_err(|error| error.to_string())
            .and_then(|json| serde_json::from_str::<AlignCase>(&json).map_err(|error| error.to_string()))
            .and_then(|case| case.validate().map(|_| case))
        {
            Ok(case) => cases.push(case),
            Err(error) => eprintln!("align list_cases: skipping {}: {error}", case_file.display()),
        }
    }
    cases.sort_by(|a, b| a.case_id.cmp(&b.case_id));
    Ok(cases)
}

/// Loads one case's images. Returns `(case, template, input)`.
pub fn load_case(root: &Path, case_id: &str) -> Result<(AlignCase, GrayImage, GrayImage), String> {
    let dir = root.join(case_id);
    let json = fs::read_to_string(dir.join(CASE_FILE)).map_err(|error| format!("Cannot read the case {case_id}: {error}"))?;
    let case: AlignCase = serde_json::from_str(&json).map_err(|error| format!("Case {case_id} is not valid JSON: {error}"))?;
    case.validate()?;
    let template = image::open(dir.join(TEMPLATE_FILE))
        .map_err(|error| format!("Cannot decode the template of {case_id}: {error}"))?
        .to_luma8();
    let input = image::open(dir.join(INPUT_FILE))
        .map_err(|error| format!("Cannot decode the input of {case_id}: {error}"))?
        .to_luma8();
    Ok((case, template, input))
}

// ---- tests: the M1 regression anchor (Plan 05 acceptance) ----

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// A 64x64 base with a corner blob + stripes: enough structure for the
    /// warp and occlusion to be observable, small enough to keep tests fast.
    fn base_image() -> GrayImage {
        let mut image = GrayImage::from_pixel(64, 64, Luma([30]));
        for y in 10..20 {
            for x in 10..20 {
                image.put_pixel(x, y, Luma([220]));
            }
        }
        for y in 0..64 {
            for x in (0..64).step_by(4) {
                image.put_pixel(x, y, Luma([180]));
            }
        }
        image
    }

    fn test_params() -> CaseParams {
        CaseParams { noise_sigma: 3.0, gain: 1.1, offset: 5.0, blur_sigma: 0.8, occlusion_ratio: 0.05, downsample: 1 }
    }

    #[test]
    fn rng_is_deterministic_and_seeded() {
        let mut a = SeededRng::new(42);
        let mut b = SeededRng::new(42);
        for _ in 0..100 {
            assert_eq!(a.next_u64(), b.next_u64());
            assert!((a.next_f64() - b.next_f64()).abs() < f64::EPSILON);
        }
        let mut c = SeededRng::new(43);
        let mut a = SeededRng::new(42);
        assert_ne!(a.next_u64(), c.next_u64());
        // gaussians: deterministic, roughly standard normal over a batch
        let mut rng = SeededRng::new(7);
        let mean: f64 = (0..1000).map(|_| rng.gaussian()).sum::<f64>() / 1000.0;
        assert!(mean.abs() < 0.15, "gaussian mean {mean} is too far from 0");
    }

    #[test]
    fn same_seed_and_params_reproduce_bytes() {
        let base = base_image();
        let params = test_params();
        let first = generate_case(&base, 2026, None, &params);
        let second = generate_case(&base, 2026, None, &params);
        assert_eq!(first.template, second.template);
        assert_eq!(first.input, second.input);
        // byte-level: the stored PNGs must be identical too
        let png = |image: &GrayImage| {
            let mut bytes = Vec::new();
            image
                .write_to(&mut std::io::Cursor::new(&mut bytes), image::ImageFormat::Png)
                .unwrap();
            bytes
        };
        assert_eq!(png(&first.input), png(&second.input));
        // a different seed must produce a different input (noise at minimum)
        let other = generate_case(&base, 2027, None, &params);
        assert_ne!(first.input, other.input);
    }

    #[test]
    fn derived_truth_is_in_range_and_pinned_truth_beats_derivation() {
        let base = base_image();
        let params = CaseParams { downsample: 2, ..CaseParams::default() };
        let case = generate_case(&base, 5, None, &params);
        assert_eq!(case.template.dimensions(), (32, 32));
        assert!(case.truth.tx_px.abs() <= 1.6 && case.truth.ty_px.abs() <= 1.6, "truth {:?}", case.truth);
        assert!(case.truth.theta_deg.abs() <= 1.5 && (case.truth.scale - 1.0).abs() <= 0.01);

        // A pinned truth must win over derivation, and the degradation stream
        // must not depend on whether the truth was pinned.
        let pinned = TruthTransform { tx_px: 3.0, ty_px: -2.0, theta_deg: 0.0, scale: 1.0 };
        let a = generate_case(&base, 9, Some(pinned.clone()), &test_params());
        let mut rng = SeededRng::new(9);
        let template = make_template(&base, &test_params());
        let b = render_input(&template, &mut rng, &pinned, &test_params());
        assert_eq!(a.input, b);
    }

    #[test]
    fn identity_truth_reproduces_the_template_without_degradations() {
        let base = base_image();
        let params = CaseParams::default();
        let case = generate_case(&base, 1, Some(TruthTransform::default()), &params);
        assert_eq!(case.input, case.template);
    }

    #[test]
    fn warp_moves_content_by_the_truth_translation() {
        // pure translation: the blob center must land exactly tx/ty away
        let template = base_image();
        let truth = TruthTransform { tx_px: 5.0, ty_px: -3.0, theta_deg: 0.0, scale: 1.0 };
        let warped = warp_transform(&template, &truth);
        let centroid = |image: &GrayImage| -> (f64, f64) {
            let mut sx = 0.0;
            let mut sy = 0.0;
            let mut n = 0.0;
            for (x, y, p) in image.enumerate_pixels() {
                if p.0[0] == 220 {
                    sx += f64::from(x);
                    sy += f64::from(y);
                    n += 1.0;
                }
            }
            (sx / n, sy / n)
        };
        let (bx, by) = centroid(&template);
        let (wx, wy) = centroid(&warped);
        // 0.25px slack: bilinear + rounding can flip a border pixel in/out of
        // the exact-220 set, nudging the centroid by a fraction of a pixel.
        assert!((wx - bx - 5.0).abs() < 0.25, "wx {wx} vs {bx}");
        assert!((wy - by + 3.0).abs() < 0.25, "wy {wy} vs {by}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn degradation_chain_is_observable() {
        let template = base_image();
        let truth = TruthTransform::default();
        // gain darkens/brightens the mean
        let mut bright = CaseParams { gain: 1.5, ..CaseParams::default() };
        let out = render_input(&template, &mut SeededRng::new(1), &truth, &bright);
        let mean = |image: &GrayImage| -> f64 { image.pixels().map(|p| f64::from(p.0[0])).sum::<f64>() / f64::from(image.pixels().count() as u32) };
        assert!(mean(&out) > mean(&template));
        // noise strictly changes pixels
        bright = CaseParams { noise_sigma: 10.0, ..CaseParams::default() };
        let noisy = render_input(&template, &mut SeededRng::new(2), &truth, &bright);
        assert_ne!(noisy, template);
        // occlusion blacks out roughly the requested fraction
        let occluded = render_input(&template, &mut SeededRng::new(3), &truth, &CaseParams { occlusion_ratio: 0.10, ..CaseParams::default() });
        let black = occluded.pixels().filter(|p| p.0[0] == 0).count();
        assert!(black > 300 && black < 700, "black px {black} for a ~10% occluder on 64x64");
    }

    #[test]
    fn case_library_round_trips_and_lists_sorted() {
        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("afvi_gen_test_{}", std::process::id()));
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
        fs::create_dir_all(&root).unwrap();

        let base = base_image();
        let case = generate_case(&base, 77, None, &test_params());
        let mut record = AlignCase::new(case_id("6AN0921", "top", 77), 77, "6AN0921", "top");
        record.truth = case.truth;
        record.params = test_params();
        record.template_path = TEMPLATE_FILE.into();
        record.input_path = INPUT_FILE.into();
        save_case(&root, &record, &case.template, &case.input).unwrap();

        // a second case under a different seed keeps the list sorted
        let case_b = generate_case(&base, 5, None, &test_params());
        let mut record_b = AlignCase::new(case_id("6AN0921", "top", 5), 5, "6AN0921", "top");
        record_b.truth = case_b.truth;
        record_b.params = test_params();
        save_case(&root, &record_b, &case_b.template, &case_b.input).unwrap();

        let listed = list_cases(&root).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(listed.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(listed[0].case_id, record_b.case_id);
        assert_eq!(listed[1].case_id, record.case_id);

        let (loaded, template, input) = load_case(&root, &record.case_id).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(loaded, record);
        assert_eq!(template, case.template);
        assert_eq!(input, case.input);

        // regeneration into the same id is idempotent
        save_case(&root, &record, &case.template, &case.input).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(list_cases(&root).unwrap().len(), 2);

        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
    }

    #[test]
    fn library_survives_a_broken_folder_and_a_missing_library() {
        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("afvi_gen_broken_{}", std::process::id()));
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
        fs::create_dir_all(root.join("damaged_case")).unwrap();
        fs::write(root.join("damaged_case").join(CASE_FILE), "{ not json").unwrap();
        fs::create_dir_all(root.join("stray")).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(list_cases(&root).unwrap().len(), 0);
        // no library at all -> empty, not an error
        assert_eq!(list_cases(&root.join("nope")).unwrap().len(), 0);
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
    }
}
````

## File: tauri-app/src-tauri/src/align/metal_sim.rs
````rust
//! Plan 07 C: simulated pre-align offset + real ROI-driven correction.
//!
//! The Metal layer is deterministically displaced (seeded translation + small
//! rotation) to fake the machine's pre-align state. The user draws ROI boxes
//! on the displaced view; the correction is computed by the REAL M5 pipeline
//! (`fiducial::verify_with_rois` - per-ROI NCC + RANSAC/Umeyama + verdict),
//! so featureless or inconsistent boxes genuinely fail. Nothing here leaks
//! the simulated truth into the fit: the seed only displaces the layer, the
//! aligner never sees it.

use super::ecc::{forward, Transform};
use super::fiducial::FiducialConfig;
use image::{GrayImage, Luma};

/// Simulated shift magnitude cap, as a fraction of the grid's short side,
/// per axis. Big enough to be obvious at a glance, small enough that one
/// ROI's local NCC search can still recover it (with the corner fiducials
/// partially clipping at the canvas edge, 3% of 2107 px measurably outran
/// the coarse match - 2% keeps the offset honest but findable).
pub const MAX_SHIFT_FRAC: f64 = 0.02;
/// Simulated rotation cap, degrees.
pub const MAX_THETA_DEG: f64 = 0.25;

/// Verdict config for CROSS-LAYER ROI matching (metal render vs median scan):
/// looser than the same-layer M5 defaults because the two modalities never
/// correlate perfectly (true-match NCC measures 0.70-0.83 on 25fbo015-15,
/// wrong-feature peaks land 0.41-0.60), but every NG gate stays - featureless
/// or inconsistent boxes still fail honestly.
pub fn sim_config() -> FiducialConfig {
    FiducialConfig {
        // covers MAX_SHIFT_FRAC plus the rotation swing at the corners
        local_search_px: 128,
        ncc_min: 0.6,
        ncc_ok: 0.7,
        ncc_ng: 0.35,
        resid_ok_px: 2.0,
        resid_ng_px: 6.0,
        ransac_inlier_px: 3.0,
        ..FiducialConfig::default()
    }
}

/// Deterministic misalignment for `seed` on a `w`×`h` grid (grid px). The
/// same seed always regenerates the same offset, so the frontend can ask for
/// "the view I let the user draw on" again when the align command runs.
/// Centre of the image is the rotation centre (same convention as
/// `ecc::forward` / the ROI fit).
pub fn offset_from_seed(seed: u64, w: u32, h: u32) -> Transform {
    let mut state = seed ^ 0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15;
    let mut next = move || {
        state ^= state << 13;
        state ^= state >> 7;
        state ^= state << 17;
        state
    };
    // -1.0 .. 1.0 per component (xorshift64 never yields 0, so % is unbiased enough)
    let unit = |next: &mut dyn FnMut() -> u64| ((next() % 2001) as f64 / 1000.0) - 1.0;
    let span = f64::from(w.min(h)) * MAX_SHIFT_FRAC;
    Transform {
        tx: unit(&mut next) * span,
        ty: unit(&mut next) * span,
        theta_deg: unit(&mut next) * MAX_THETA_DEG,
        scale: 1.0,
    }
}

/// Inverse of a similarity under the `ecc::forward` convention
/// (`q = c + s·R(θ)·(p−c) + t`), so `forward(invert(t), ·)` undoes `t`.
pub fn invert(t: &Transform) -> Transform {
    let theta = t.theta_deg.to_radians();
    let (sin, cos) = (theta.sin(), theta.cos());
    Transform {
        tx: -(t.tx * cos + t.ty * sin) / t.scale,
        ty: -(-t.tx * sin + t.ty * cos) / t.scale,
        theta_deg: -t.theta_deg,
        scale: 1.0 / t.scale,
    }
}

/// Displaces `layer` by `t` (content moves, canvas stays): output(q) samples
/// the layer at `forward(t)⁻¹(q)`, bilinear, black outside. This is both how
/// the simulated misalignment is produced and how the fitted correction is
/// applied afterwards (the fit maps displaced-layer coords -> median coords).
pub fn warp_layer(layer: &GrayImage, t: &Transform) -> GrayImage {
    let (w, h) = (layer.width() as usize, layer.height() as usize);
    let (cx, cy) = (w as f64 / 2.0, h as f64 / 2.0);
    let inv = invert(t);
    let buf = layer.as_raw().clone();
    let mut out = GrayImage::from_pixel(w as u32, h as u32, Luma([0]));
    for y in 0..h {
        for x in 0..w {
            let (sx, sy) = forward(&inv, cx, cy, x as f64, y as f64);
            if let Some(v) = sample_bilinear(&buf, w, h, sx, sy) {
                out.put_pixel(x as u32, y as u32, Luma([v]));
            }
        }
    }
    out
}

fn sample_bilinear(buf: &[u8], w: usize, h: usize, x: f64, y: f64) -> Option<u8> {
    if x < -1.0 || y < -1.0 || x > w as f64 || y > h as f64 {
        return None;
    }
    let (x0, y0) = (x.floor() as i64, y.floor() as i64);
    let (fx, fy) = (x - x0 as f64, y - y0 as f64);
    let at = |px: i64, py: i64| -> Option<f64> {
        if px < 0 || py < 0 || px >= w as i64 || py >= h as i64 {
            return None;
        }
        Some(f64::from(buf[py as usize * w + px as usize]))
    };
    let p00 = at(x0, y0)?;
    let p10 = at(x0 + 1, y0).unwrap_or(p00);
    let p01 = at(x0, y0 + 1).unwrap_or(p00);
    let p11 = at(x0 + 1, y0 + 1).unwrap_or(p00);
    let top = p00 * (1.0 - fx) + p10 * fx;
    let bottom = p01 * (1.0 - fx) + p11 * fx;
    Some((top * (1.0 - fy) + bottom * fy).round() as u8)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn dot_at(x: u32, y: u32) -> GrayImage {
        let mut img = GrayImage::from_pixel(100, 80, Luma([0]));
        img.put_pixel(x, y, Luma([255]));
        img
    }

    #[test]
    fn offset_is_deterministic_per_seed_and_bounded() {
        let a = offset_from_seed(42, 3072, 2117);
        let b = offset_from_seed(42, 3072, 2117);
        assert_eq!(a, b, "same seed, same offset");
        let others: Vec<_> = (0..20).map(|s| offset_from_seed(1000 + s, 3072, 2117)).collect();
        assert!(others.iter().any(|t| *t != a), "seeds actually vary");
        for t in [a].into_iter().chain(others) {
            assert!(t.tx.abs() <= 3072f64.min(2117f64) * MAX_SHIFT_FRAC + 1e-9);
            assert!(t.ty.abs() <= 3072f64.min(2117f64) * MAX_SHIFT_FRAC + 1e-9);
            assert!(t.theta_deg.abs() <= MAX_THETA_DEG + 1e-9);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn warp_moves_content_by_the_offset_and_correction_undoes_it() {
        // translate +10 x: the dot at (50,50) lands on (60,50)
        let off = Transform { tx: 10.0, ty: 0.0, theta_deg: 0.0, scale: 1.0 };
        let displaced = warp_layer(&dot_at(50, 50), &off);
        assert_eq!(displaced.get_pixel(60, 50).0[0], 255);
        assert_eq!(displaced.get_pixel(50, 50).0[0], 0);

        // the ROI fit maps displaced -> nominal, i.e. it is the INVERSE of the
        // simulated offset; applying it puts the dot back
        let corrected = warp_layer(&displaced, &invert(&off));
        assert_eq!(corrected.get_pixel(50, 50).0[0], 255);
        assert_eq!(corrected.get_pixel(60, 50).0[0], 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn invert_twice_is_identity_and_rotation_warp_stays_sharp_enough() {
        let t = Transform { tx: 7.0, ty: -3.0, theta_deg: 0.4, scale: 1.0 };
        let back = invert(&invert(&t));
        assert!((back.tx - t.tx).abs() < 1e-9);
        assert!((back.ty - t.ty).abs() < 1e-9);
        assert!((back.theta_deg - t.theta_deg).abs() < 1e-9);

        // a solid block survives a max-strength warp with its centre white
        let mut block = GrayImage::from_pixel(200, 200, Luma([0]));
        for y in 80..120 {
            for x in 80..120 {
                block.put_pixel(x, y, Luma([255]));
            }
        }
        let off = offset_from_seed(7, 200, 200);
        let warped = warp_layer(&block, &off);
        assert_eq!(warped.get_pixel(100, 100).0[0], 255, "centre stays put under rotation about centre");
    }
}
````
